source.author: cic
source.text: Verum ut aliquando ad causas deducamus illum, quem constituimus, et eas quidem, in quibus plusculum negoti est, iudiciorum atque litiumriserit aliquis fortasse hoc praeceptum; est enim non tam acutum quam necessarium magisque monitoris non fatui quam eruditi magistrihoc ei primum praecipiemus, quascumque causas erit tractaturus, ut eas diligenter penitusque cognoscat.
source.text_original: Verum ut aliquando ad causas deducamus illum, quem constituimus, et eas quidem, in quibus plusculum negoti est, iudiciorum atque litium—riserit aliquis fortasse hoc praeceptum; est enim non tam acutum quam necessarium magisque monitoris non fatui quam eruditi magistri—hoc ei primum praecipiemus, quascumque causas erit tractaturus, ut eas diligenter penitusque cognoscat.
source.text_english: But in order that we may at last bring that man, whom we have set before us, down to actual cases—and indeed to those in which there is a bit more business involved—someone may perhaps laugh at this precept in lawsuits and trials; for it is not so much clever as necessary, and more the warning of a sensible counselor than the teaching of a learned master. We shall first enjoin this upon him: whatever cases he is going to handle, let him understand them thoroughly and in depth.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: hoc enim et Tullius tuus et ante illum in breui et solo uolumine scribit Antonius, primam causae esse uictoriam diligenter causam, pro qua dicturus es, discere.
reuse.text_original: hoc enim et Tullius tuus et ante illum in breui et solo uolumine scribit Antonius, primam causae esse uictoriam diligenter causam, pro qua dicturus es, discere.
reuse.text_english: For this your Tully too, and before him Antonius in a brief and single volume, write that the first victory of a case is to learn carefully the case for which you are going to speak.
